summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update43.json → valid=true). Final strengthening of the verification finding with a requirement anchor from the shipped documentation: the leader-write list in docs/README.md describes VerifyLeader as sending a heartbeat to all voters to confirm the peer is still the leader (docs/README.md:44-49), and the thread walkthrough lists the verification request among the leader loop's inputs (86-96), while the membership document defines a non-voter as a member excluded from elections and commitment. Against that, the implementation registers the pending verification with every replication state — one exists for every configured peer except the local server, regardless of suffrage — and counts each acknowledgement without checking who sent it, against a threshold computed from the voters. Recorded as one Fact plus a successor interpretation for the same question (earlier opinions and counterevidence preserved) with the split made explicit: the deviation is now established from the captured material itself — documented audience is voters, actual audience is every configured peer — while only the consequence remains conditional, because the window in which a leader can pass such a verification while unreachable from every voter is bounded by the lease check, which does count voters and steps the leader down within the lease, so a stale read needs either that window or a long lease among the configurations validation permits. Counterevidence kept honest: the documentation line is a one-sentence orientation summary rather than a formal specification; the lease check remains an independent voter-based backstop; a caller combining verification with the documented lease assumption carries the exposure any lease-based read has; and nothing was executed. This closes my work on the run, whose budget is now exhausted — no stop declaration is made, since that boundary belongs to the controller.
